solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Work hard when dam is neglected?

definitions.text: Work hard when dam is neglected?

parts.words: Work hard when dam is neglected?
parts.note: a beaver builds dams; one that has left its dam is literally away, and the phrase also means to toil diligently

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads two ways: the idiom for working steadily, and a dam-building animal absent from its dam.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to toil persistently and industriously at a task, like the famously busy rodent.

clue.text: Curse I uttered after running back

indicators.note: after places the spoken I behind the turned word
back means the word for running is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a machine that is running is live

indicators.note: uttered means the letter I is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter I spoken sounds like the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone casting a hex while fleeing backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' means live, as a live wire is running; the 'I' is the speaker's pronoun in the surface but a letter spoken aloud in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a malevolent glance believed to bring misfortune, i.e. a hex.

indicators.note: detailed read as de-tailed: the official's last letter is cut off

parts.note: a verger is a church official who looks after the building

explanation.surface: A functionary has set out precisely where a border runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'precise' but means the tail is removed: VERGER loses its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is an edge or border, such as the grass strip at the side of a road.

clue.text: Local team score at either end

indicators.note: at either end means the word for score is split to sit on both sides of the team

parts.note: to score is to cut or tear, as is rent
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A local side scoring at both ends of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like points in a match but is a scratch or tear; 'Local' is a noun here, a person who lives nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a local is someone who lives in the area, an inhabitant.

clue.text: Regional dish cooked in Winchester with lemon zest and endive tips

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed up like ingredients

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tips are the first letters of lemon, zest and endive

explanation.surface: A recipe from a Hampshire kitchen with citrus and salad garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the fodder rather than linking: IN + WINCHESTER + L, Z, E rearranged. Winchester is an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: The breaded veal cutlet is the signature dish of Vienna, so it is a specialty of a particular place.

clue.text: Queen attends royal house for ball

indicators.note: attends means the queen accompanies the house, coming next to it

parts.note: York is an English royal house
ER, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviates Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch visiting a royal residence for a formal dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance but is a cricket delivery: a yorker is pitched right at the batter's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a delivery aimed to land at the batsman's feet, a type of bowled ball.

indicators.note: occupied by means the moon's name holds the British letters inside it

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons
GB, Great Britain, abbreviates British

explanation.surface: A satellite colonised by Britons.
explanation.definitionFit: The Igbo are an ethnic group of south-eastern Nigeria.

clue.text: I will get a flirt uncomfortable

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll
a tease is a flirt

explanation.surface: Someone admits a coquette will make them squirm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes feeling awkward or uneasy in a situation.

clue.text: British spy and Commonwealth soldier nearly got jackpot

indicators.note: nearly means each name stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional British spy
an Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps

explanation.surface: 007 and an Aussie soldier almost scoop a big prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' serves both names: BOND loses D and ANZAC loses C.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a sudden great windfall of wealth, like a large prize win.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a row or rank, one of several stacked layers
second meaning: one who ties things

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a whimsical agent noun: one who ties.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a layer or rank, and a tier is also, jokingly, somebody fastening knots.

clue.text: Insist surgeon firstly put on mask

indicators.note: firstly means only the opening letter of surgeon is taken

parts.note: to put on clothing is to wear it
a blind is a mask or screen hiding something

explanation.surface: A surgeon is told to don a face covering before operating.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear blind is to assert something emphatically and repeatedly.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., the bottom of a leg
second meaning: a spy's ... is the cover story behind an assumed identity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' splits as LEG END; in espionage a legend is the invented biography that supports a false identity.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence services call an agent's fabricated backstory a legend, and the bottom of a limb is its end.

indicators.note: takes means the evening holds the time letter inside it

parts.note: evening is the time after dark

explanation.surface: A night-time equestrian outing runs long.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is an equestrian competition combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

parts.note: egging (on) means urging
S abbreviates small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A judge encourages wearing little trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeggings are stretchy leggings styled to look like denim jeans, a kind of legwear.

clue.text: Happy pilot released a very old fighter

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: released means the pilot lets go of the letters for a and very

parts.note: an aviator is a pilot

explanation.surface: A cheerful airman, freed, is an ancient warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released' takes A and V (a very) out of AVIATOR, leaving IATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators were armed combatants in ancient Roman arenas.

parts.note: a way, as in a way of doing it, is a knack or trick

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a card player losing a trick; 'a trick' is A + WAY, a method or knack.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone away is absent, not present, just as missing means.

clue.text: Parts of army, not married, made to occupy warships

indicators.note: to occupy means the shortened word goes inside the warships

parts.note: brigs are two-masted sailing warships

indicators.note: not means the married letter is left out of made

explanation.surface: Unmarried sailors are posted aboard fighting ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not married' removes M from MADE, giving ADE, which goes into BRIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit, a subdivision of an army.

indicators.note: first means the toilet word comes before a

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory, a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone boasts the toilet comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' is part of the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lava is molten rock flowing from a volcano.

clue.text: Greed is a depravity without a recognised origin

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside: vice goes round the letters

parts.note: vice means depravity

indicators.note: origin means the opening letter of recognised

explanation.surface: Greed is called a vice lacking any known source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so VICE wraps A + R, giving VARICE after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, a synonym of covetousness.

indicators.note: beastly means rotten or awful, so the letters are badly treated and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty or meaty bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like part of the description, but it signals rearranging OR FLESHY.
explanation.definitionFit: The horsefly is a large biting fly that pesters livestock.

indicators.note: deleted means the island letter is struck out

parts.note: ambient means surrounding

explanation.surface: A shining coastline around an island has been erased.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that glows softly or flickers, hence shining.

indicators.note: nets means the silicon symbol catches the other word inside

parts.note: Si is the chemical symbol for silicon
camp means affected or exaggerated in manner

explanation.surface: Chip-filled fishing nets have tainted a catch of shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' is a verb: SI catches CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines or large prawns, usually served breaded.

clue.text: Is slice of calamari a Chinese or Mexican tradition?

indicators.note: slice of means the answer is cut from the run of words

explanation.surface: Asks whether squid rings with a Chinese dish are a Mexican custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi is the traditional folk music of Mexico, played by strolling bands.

clue.text: Shelter from snow after I shook off my cold

indicators.note: shook off means the letter I is shed from the shelter

parts.note: an igloo is a shelter built from snow
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from a chill after leaving their snow hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from snow' belongs with 'Shelter', not a separate instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold in the sense of cheerless and dismal is close to gloomy.

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
dour means stern and austere

explanation.surface: A romance with a stern personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean reputation or standing, as in being in good odour, i.e. one's character.

clue.text: American defrauded two men with one final letter

parts.note: Vic and Tim are two men's names
I is the Roman numeral one
zed is the name of z, the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Two chaps team up with a last character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' marks the Z spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be victimised is to be cheated or swindled; the -ize spelling is the US form.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a portent or token of the future
second meaning: a hen party is women only, so it has O (zero) MEN

explanation.walkthrough: A hen party is a pre-wedding celebration for the bride and her female friends; the question mark flags the split reading O MEN, nought men.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent of something to come, and an all-female gathering has nil males.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rip in fabric

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses with different pronunciations: a drop from the eye and a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a single bead of liquid, while a rip in cloth is also this word.

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A decoration chosen to flatter a tall statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a sculpture but signals the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate a book is to adorn or decorate it with pictures.
